newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes off, Cabinda said traded into China.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes off, Cabinda said traded into China.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were generally lower on Tuesday in line with the wider global market as Cabinda and Nemba crude were said traded into China.
There was no immediate confirmation of the deals, but traders said the market was widely talking three or four Cabinda/Nemba crude deals to Unipec and other Chinese players.
The lifting dates ranged from prompt November to first decade December with prices dated Brent -$1.80 to -$1.60.
The sellers included a French major and a Wall Street trader, market sources said.
The focus on West African grades reflected the widening contango at the front of the Brent market and the narrowing of the Brent/Dubai.
December Brent/Dubai was assessed notionally at $1.82/$1.95 in Singapore and January at $1.92/$1.96.
Although a spread just below $2.00 is not a clear signal of an open arbitrage, traders said the weakness of the Brent market had made the economics possible.
Dated Brent was assessed around -30 cents per barrel, and the November/December spread around minus seven cents.
Traders were assessing the official selling prices of Gulf grades.
The Oman differential to published Dubai prices came in to 74 cents from 78 cents, reflected last month's expectations of a falling Oman spread.
However, ADNOC premiums over Dubai widened, reflecting the strength of market premiums during December trading.
Murban stretched out to $2.04, Lower Zakum to $2.09 and Umm Shaif to $1.79 for January barrels from a month-earlier $1.88, $1.93 and $1.58 respectively.
